summary: Battles now run in real time on a battlefield. Heroes follow Strength, Agility and Intelligence, and armour is flat. There is a balance pass, new art for all creatures and heroes, and a story with 9 scenes. This list covers v0.5.1, v0.5.2 and v0.6.

highlights.title: Real-time battle
highlights.text: Heroes and monsters run, aim and fight on a battlefield. There are no turns.

highlights.title: Attributes and flat armour
highlights.text: Strength, Agility and Intelligence replace Skill and Magic. Armour takes points off each hit.

highlights.title: Story
highlights.text: Nine scenes follow your first chapter, from the first hero to the road east.

groups.heading: Real-time battle
items: Heroes and monsters move on a battlefield, 36 long and 8 deep. Melee units run to their target. Archers, Mages and Priests hit from a distance.
A unit attacks the nearest enemy. It stands still while it attacks or casts.
Attack time replaces Speed. Agility and gear make it shorter. Haste and Slow share the same pool.
Boots add movement speed. Ranged classes run at 80% of the speed of melee classes.

groups.heading: Attributes and damage
items: Heroes have Strength, Agility and Intelligence. Skill and Magic are gone.
Health follows Strength (14.6 for each point). Magic resist follows Intelligence (0.2 for each point). Armour comes only from class base values and gear.
Damage = class base + primary attribute + weapon.
Armour and Magic resist are flat. A hit = attack x swing x spell power x critical multiplier - armour, and never less than 1.
Critical chance is 4% for every unit. Critical damage is 200%. Resource pools are fixed: 30 Mana, 28 Stamina, 24 Hatred and 26 Rage.
Mana Shield absorbs a flat amount plus a share of the maximum health.

groups.heading: Balance
items: Monsters use a table of anchors for each level, and each monster has a stat factor. Monsters have an attack time between 1.0 and 2.0 seconds.
The Goblin Chief has 1,600 health, 148 damage, 19 armour and 8 Magic resist. Crushing Cleaver waits 12 seconds.
Level 1 kills give more experience. A hero needs 380 experience for level 2.
Weapon damage grows by a flat amount for each item level. Armour gives Armour and Magic resist, not health.
Each upgrade level adds 1 to the main stat, or 5% of it on a strong item. The upgrade chances are higher.
Crafter levels 1 to 8 use a fixed experience table. A crafter gains at most 2 levels from one craft while below level 2.
Set recipes open at the same crafter level as the basic recipe. Weapons that open at crafter level 1 have no set recipe.
The Toadskin set gives +25 health. The Spider Silk set gives +2 attack speed. The Sharp Fang set gives +2 Agility.

groups.heading: Gear
items: New affixes: Swift, Vital, Robust, Keen, Savage, Vampiric, Brisk, Brutal, Wise, Stalwart and Blessed.
Gear can add attack speed, critical chance, critical damage, life steal and movement speed. These are percent points.
Woodworking is now Enchanting, and a new Leatherworking crafter makes hide armour and belts.

groups.heading: Story
items: Nine story scenes play in chapter 1: the first hero, the second hero, each dungeon, and the end of the chapter.
After chapter 1, the people of the castle have new things to say.

groups.heading: Screens
items: Hero stat labels, and an equip preview in the backpack that shows the change of each stat.
A wide view option shows more of the town on a narrow screen.
Town people talk about your company, your gear and the time of day.
The town has fewer buildings, so it is easier to cross.

groups.heading: Sound and art
items: All creatures and all hero portraits are drawn again. The Goblin Chief is a big boss sprite.
New music data for the town, the battle and the story.

sections.title: Known issues
sections.intro: These problems are known and are not fixed in this version.

groups.heading: Game
items: The balance scenarios did not run for this version, so the numbers are not checked.
The new pictures and sounds are not checked by eye and ear yet.
Priest, Thief, Barbarian and Fighter have placeholder numbers.
